 Thousands of Winnipeggers head downtown to see Santa | CBC News Loaded Manitoba Thousands of Winnipeggers head downtown to see Santa
 The Manitoba Hydro Santa Claus parade rolled through the heart of the city, with dozens of groups and organizations participating. First Santa Claus parade since Manitoba ended daylight saving time, leading to brighter views
 CBC News · Posted: Nov 15, 2026 1:39 PM EST | Last Updated: November 15 Play Listen to this article Estimated 2 minutes The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results. Santa Claus waves to spectators during the Santa Claus Parade on Nov. 14 in Winnipeg. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/Radio-Canada) Social Sharing
 Thousands of people gathered in downtown Winnipeg on Saturday to catch a glimpse of Santa Claus's return to the city. 
 The Manitoba Hydro Santa Claus parade rolled through the heart of the city, with dozens of groups and organizations participating. 
 Starting at Portage Avenue and Main Street, decorated floats, volunteers in costume  and the big man himself headed west on the parade route before turning south on Memorial, and ending on St. Mary Avenue. 
 Established in 1909 by Eaton’s Department Store, the Santa Claus Parade has been a Winnipeg tradition for well over 100 years. 
 Stéphane Deniset and his young daughter, Lucille, watching the Santa Claus parade at the corner of Portage Avenue and Main Street. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/CBC Radio-Canada)
 This is the first Santa Claus parade in Winnipeg since the province decided to end daylight saving time, resulting in part of the parade, which usually starts after sunset, being a little bit brighter.
 The extra hours of sunlight weren't a problem for Stéphane Deniset and his daughter, Lucille, who are regular participants in the parade. 
 "It takes away some of the light on the trucks, but it doesn't take away the celebration," Deniset told CBC Radio-Canada. 
 Logan Lyons watches the Santa Claus parade from her father Tyler Lyons' shoulders on Saturday. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/CBC Radio-Canada)
 It also didn't make getting to see Santa any less exciting for Logan Lyons, who attended the parade with her dad, Tyler.
 "I love Santa Claus!" she said.   
 Dozens of organizations decorated floats to participate in the Santa Claus Parade on Saturday. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/CBC Radio-Canada)
 Decorated floats and volunteers in costume took part in Winnipeg's Santa Claus Parade Saturday. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/CBC Radio-Canada)
 Organizations added some Christmas cheer to vehicles taking part in the Santa Claus parade. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/CBC Radio-Canada)
 Volunteers in the parade, including this elf, distributed candy to kids watching from the sidelines. (Graham Sceviour-Fraehlich/CBC Radio-Canada)
